reviews.text:
I stayed in Room 4036 to celebrate my birthday with my family, and unfortunately, it turned into one of the worst hotel experiences we’ve ever had.

The hotel never disclosed on its website or before check-in that major construction was taking place. We only found out after arriving, and to make matters worse, we were assigned to Room 4036, which was directly next to the construction area.

I immediately spoke with the front desk and was told the construction would end at 5:00 PM. Instead, it continued until around 6:00 PM. The next morning, construction started again at 6:00 AM, waking up our entire family, including our young children.

The front desk’s response was very dismissive. They simply said they would let the manager know, but nothing was done. There was no apology, no offer to move us to another room, and no attempt to make up for the situation.

For a luxury resort charging premium rates, this is completely unacceptable. If construction is taking place, guests should be informed before booking, and no one should be assigned to Room 4036 or any room directly next to the construction.

I have attached videos showing the construction noise as evidence. This stay completely ruined what was supposed to be a special birthday celebration. It was absolutely not worth the price we paid, and I would not recommend staying here.

Our family’s experience at The Phoenician was incredibly disappointing and frankly unacceptable. During our stay, our children became seriously ill with food poisoning after eating at the resort, leading to multiple trips to the Emergency Room Well, on vacation in an unfamiliar area.

What made an already terrible situation even worse was how the resort chose to handle it. Instead of taking direct accountability or working with us in good faith to resolve such a serious matter, The Phoenician immediately pushed everything off onto their insurance company. This felt less like an effort to help and more like an attempt to shield themselves from responsibility while allowing the insurance provider to play the “bad guy” by denying our claim.

Now, because of that denial, we are left facing substantial medical bills, while our regular health insurance will not cover many of the costs. Rather than standing behind their guests after a serious incident, the resort’s approach appeared designed to distance itself from responsibility and avoid owning what happened.

For a property that prides itself on luxury and service, this lack of accountability was shocking. When your children’s health is impacted, you expect compassion, responsibility, and action—not corporate deflection. Our experience left us feeling abandoned, frustrated, and deeply let down.

reviews.text:
We had the pleasure of staying at the The Phoenician last month and thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

The resort itself is aesthetically beautiful, with an impressive range of activities and spaces for both families and adults. Multiple pools, several restaurants, recreational options, and quiet nooks throughout the property make it a destination where nearly everyone can find a place to relax.

What stood out most, however, was the service, particularly at check-in. Christian noticed that we shared a somewhat uncommon last name and took a few extra moments to genuinely get to know us. He made the arrival process effortless, but what happened later truly surprised us. When we returned to our room that evening, we found a heartfelt handwritten welcome note along with special snacks and a thoughtfully prepared margarita cocktail ensemble.

That level of personalization is increasingly rare today, especially in an era where staffing shortages often leave guests feeling rushed through transactional interactions. Experiences like this are a reminder that service is personal and meaningful, and that organizations capable of delivering it consistently likely invest well in their people and culture.

The rooms were well-appointed, the beds comfortable, and the bathrooms spacious and functional. As someone who admittedly notices details like water pressure, I can report that it was more than adequate. The on-site restaurants offered a nice variety of options, and the servers throughout the resort clearly understood what genuine hospitality looks like. The Tavern in particular was lively and enjoyable, with good live music and excellent service.

A couple of practical notes for future guests: reservations are highly recommended for the restaurants. The seating process can feel a bit cumbersome, with multiple hand-offs even during slower periods. Additionally, poolside service could be more attentive at times, as we occasionally needed to flag staff down.

That said, those issues were minor compared to the overall experience. While five stars may feel slightly generous given the price point and a few operational inefficiencies, on a 1–10 scale this resort is a very solid 9/10 and absolutely worthy of consideration for anyone visiting Scottsdale.

I would expect that after calling more than once to rectify the charges I would have received a call with at least an explanation of the charges . I believe this was a mix up with how our work team set up payments for breakfasts ( using coupons ) and staff accidentally charging it to my room. BE WARNED !

Pros:
Great food
Beautiful scenery of Camelback mountain
Comfortable beds, quiet nights
Staff willing to take you across the resort on golf carts

The pool was not crowded and yet the staff were barely visible -- leaving used towels and food (which attracted birds) around the pool area.  Otherwise a great trip.

reviews.text: Gary at the Phoenician spa is a great listener and amazing massage therapist. He helped my knee after acl surgery without any pain and was extremely responsive of any areas of caution I needed.

reviews.text: Anniversary Trip|For years, we’ve been intending to go to The Phoenician when we had an opportunity to celebrate and so we decided to go on our 32nd wedding anniversary. Upon arrival, the staff was certainly nice but seemed like there weren’t enough of them. After flying from the East Coast and a pretty long travel day, I think there were four people in line to be checked in and only one of the six registration desk in operation. We did not arrive at a weird time. It was in the middle of the afternoon about the time check-in’s were starting. Our room was as expected very nice, clean pretty contemporary. The amenities in the bathroom were very nice. During our stay, we ate at multiple of the food outlets the pool bar and the fast casual alternative were unremarkable. Fine but not necessarily what you might expect at one of the nicer hotels. We did eat at the steakhouse and it was a fantastic experience. The service was what you would expect and the food was even better. Our primary purpose for this trip was just to enjoy the Scottsdale weather and sun and so the pool was the focus of our trip and we were very disappointed. We did not use the upper pool. It was mostly family oriented, and there seemed to be a lot going on and everybody having a good time, we focused on the adult pool and then what they call the mother of pearl Pool the mother pearl pool was all ages pool and early in the morning was very nice and mostly clean, we spent the bulk of our time at the adult pool, which was very lacking. The pool itself was very old and dated the tiles had a thick layer of scum on them and the pool felt just generally dirty. The water was cloudy and it seemed as though wasn’t being very well cared for. To be fair the pool deck service people did an excellent job keeping you hydrated offering new fresh towels, willingness to help you move your chairs and keep yourself covered under umbrellas. It was more of facilities problem than a service problem. If you were going to this hotel for a pool experience, I would choose another. I cannot speak to the golf tennis and spa facilities. They all look very nice and people seem to be having a very good time but as for a pool trip, we were disappointed.

reviews.text: Can’t put my finger on what it was exactly but something was off. We arrived and were able to check in and get into our room at 9:30am which was awesome! When we got there, there was a candy bar rapper, and some papers on the dresser. Later that night, when we went to use the bathtub, the drain did not work so water constantly drained out of the tub while you were in it. The worst part was the air conditioning was not working. It would get cold but then in the middle of the night AC would shut off and my husband and I would be sweating and have to take all the blankets off. This happened multiple times. The pool staff was awesome and the food by the pool was fantastic. However, the pools themselves did not feel very clean. There was so much hair at the bottom of the pool and my husband and I kept getting wads of hair stuck between our toes, they sell pool cleaners… those should be ran every single night. We had an extremely disappointing meal at the Mowrey restaurant. My husband‘s food was cold and the flavor was awful. We have been to some really nice resorts and hotels around the world. I guess with this being a five star resort and how much people love it I was expecting a little more attention to detail and cleanliness. There was a lot of wear and tear. You could tell around the doors and light switches and everything just needed a little facelift. For the price you pay I was very surprised by the way some of the main bathrooms looked. One of the sinks by the pool  was clogged the whole time and cloudy brown water was sitting in it. The doors looked like a campground site with raccoon claws trying to get out of the bathroom… it was interesting.

reviews.text:
We had a really enjoyable stay at The Phoenician overall, with several standout moments that made the experience memorable.

First, housekeeping was excellent—our room was consistently spotless, refreshed on time, and maintained to a high standard throughout our stay. That level of attention definitely added to the comfort and luxury feel of the resort.

A special thank you to Bradley at the concierge desk, who was absolutely fantastic—knowledgeable, attentive, and genuinely invested in making sure we had a great experience. Another concierge team member (I believe her name started with “S”) was also very helpful and pleasant, contributing to the overall great service we received in that area.

The only downside during our stay was an interaction with a young lady handling room service calls, which did not reflect the level of service expected at a resort of this caliber. However, we appreciated that the front desk manager addressed the concern promptly and professionally, restoring the level of service we anticipated.

Overall, a beautiful property with excellent service recovery and standout staff—would definitely return.
reviews.author: EDRICA RICHARDSON

reviews.text:
Our spring break at the Phoenician was nothing short of extraordinary—truly one of the most memorable family trips we’ve ever had. From the moment we arrived, we were welcomed with warmth, professionalism, and a level of care that made us feel completely at home.

A special thank you to Sherry at breakfast, who made every morning such a joy. She went above and beyond to make sure our kids were happy and well taken care of, always greeting us with a smile and remembering the little details that made our experience feel personal and special. Breakfast quickly became one of our favorite parts of the day because of her.

Price at the front desk was equally incredible. He made check-in seamless and set the tone for our stay with his friendly, attentive service. Anytime we had a question or needed assistance, he handled it with genuine kindness and efficiency. It’s clear he takes pride in creating a great guest experience.

And we absolutely cannot say enough about the staff at the hotel pools. They were phenomenal—always attentive, upbeat, and so patient with families. Whether it was helping us find the perfect spot, keeping things running smoothly, or just adding to the fun atmosphere, they made our pool days unforgettable for both us and our kids.

The entire property is stunning, the amenities are top-notch, and the service is consistently exceptional. What really sets the Phoenician apart, though, is the people. Every single staff member we encountered made us feel valued and cared for.

We left already talking about when we can come back. Thank you for an incredible spring break—we’ll be recommending this place to everyone we know!
reviews.author: Colleen Clarke

reviews.text:
We stayed here for our spring break, and it was truly one of the most amazing places we’ve ever experienced. From the moment we arrived, everything felt top-notch—this is a true five-star resort in every sense. The property is absolutely stunning, with beautifully maintained grounds, luxurious amenities, and an atmosphere that perfectly blends elegance with relaxation. Every detail—from the rooms to the service—was impeccable.
I can’t say enough good things about our stay. This is easily one of the most beautiful Marriott properties we’ve visited, and we would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a memorable, upscale getaway. We can’t wait to come back!
reviews.author: Arteida Bickford

reviews.text: We had a poor experience checking in but I have to say the manager whose name is Price went above and beyond to make things up to us. He was a gentleman and he is the reason I would come back. He’s a true professional and did a great job with us.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Denha

reviews.text:
Nothing about this hotel is luxury. 4 star at best. We arrived to our interconnecting rooms and walked straight back out. In what can only be compared to a motel block, the carpet was taped down with black masking tape, stains over furniture, general signs of years of wear and tear were hugely obvious. Even our balcony had some sort of juice stain that hadn’t been cleaned from the previous guests. We went back to reception to tell them we were changing hotels when they suddenly found us interconnecting rooms in the main hotel (previously unavailable). Whilst still a far stretch from what we would consider luxury - especially for close to $1000 per night per room - these were better than our previous option. Douglas agreed to modify the rate too - thank goodness because we’d have been sick paying what we’d originally committed to.

However the disappointment didn’t end there. Discarded glasses and rubbish decorate communal areas. Staircases and outdoor areas haven’t had a thorough sweep or wipe down for what looks like months. Pool loungers are very uncomfortable with thin basic towels. There is a queue for breakfast everyday and you’re unable to make reservations. Free coffee machines and milk canisters are often found empty. Asked for an ice coffee at the pool but apparently this isn’t on offer and I have to go into one of the restaurants to see if they might serve it - this would be totally acceptable for a hotel that doesn’t claim to be 5 star luxury.

Staff are friendly enough, but most don’t go over and above. I can only assume lacking a manager who is experienced in what 5 star luxury actually means. It appears other recent reviews emulate our experience and I only wish we had studied  these before making our reservation.

Kids were happy enough with tennis and pool areas. But unless this hotel has a huge overhaul, its increasingly negative reputation will get the better of it.

reviews.author: Dustin LaFavre

reviews.text:
My husband and I chose The Phoenician for a mini-honeymoon, using a large number of Marriott points with the expectation of an exceptional, elevated experience. Based on its “luxury” branding and AAA Five Diamond status, we arrived genuinely excited. Unfortunately, that excitement quickly turned into confusion and disappointment.

I’m still struggling to understand how this property maintains a 4-star rating. The gap between what was advertised and what was delivered was…impressive.

The room itself was perfectly average. Not offensive, but not memorable either. If someone told me it was a standard 2 or 3 star hotel room, I wouldn’t question it. The balcony was nice, but certainly not enough to justify the “luxury” label.

Where things really fell apart though was the service.

Standard housekeeping was not provided. Over a 6-day stay, despite calling and even going to the front desk in person, we never received a proper room cleaning. At one point, someone stopped by, made the bed, and dropped off towels…while leaving behind dirty wine glasses and trash. An interesting interpretation of “service.” It gets better. Later that same day, a bottle of champagne and fruit were delivered as a congratulatory honeymoon gift (a thoughtful gesture). However, it was placed right alongside the same uncollected garbage, which made the experience feel more way more awkward than celebratory.

Fast forward to when we eventually ran out of toilet paper, we had to walk to the front desk to ask for more. At that point, it genuinely felt like we might as well have packed our own. What stood out most wasn’t just the inconvenience—it was how completely unfazed the staff seemed and how they handled it - with lack of urgency or apology.

At the pool, we ordered hummus that took an hour to arrive. After asking a waitress, it was pretty clear the order had been forgotten. Again, things happen—but the food finally arrived undercooked and underwhelming.

Ironically, the only smooth experiences we had were the ones we paid extra for—like the $450 cabana. And to be fair, the golf cart staff were excellent and easily the highlight of the service we encountered.

Thankfully, we spent much of our time off-property hiking and kayaking, which ended up being the best part of the trip, likely because it meant less time dealing with the hotel.

I don’t typically write reviews, but this experience was too disappointing to ignore. When you market yourself as a luxury property, the expectation isn’t perfection—it’s basic hospitality paired with elevated service. Unfortunately, this stay delivered neither.

The worst part about this entire experience has actually been having to relive it by writing this review. But my intention is to save others from having to go through a similar experience.

We had an absolutely incredible experience at The Phoenician—truly a five-star stay from start to finish.

A very special thank you to Allie, Lolita, Emma, and Cameo, who supported us through every phase of planning—from months before our arrival all the way through departure. Coordinating a group trip of 45 people is no small undertaking, and their attention to detail, responsiveness, and professionalism ensured everything went off without a hitch. They genuinely went above and beyond in every possible way.

The property itself is stunning, and the level of service is truly next-level across the board.

We’d also like to recognize Max, who did an outstanding job organizing a large group of us for a Saturday morning golf outing, making the experience seamless and enjoyable for everyone. Erica was equally fantastic in arranging our cabana rentals—thanks to her thoughtful planning and recommendations, we had an unforgettable pool party day that our entire group is still talking about.

Overall, this was one of the best group travel experiences we’ve ever had. Every single person in our group loved the resort, and we are so grateful to the entire team at The Phoenician for making it so memorable. We cannot wait to return!

reviews.text:
I recently stayed at the hotel and had a really positive experience. From the moment I arrived, check-in was smooth and welcoming.

What stood out most during my stay was Sara, who took care of my room. She came twice a day and did an exceptional job. She was incredibly kind, organized, and thoughtful. She didn’t just clean the room - she paid attention to the little things. She neatly organized my belongings, kept everything spotless, and was very respectful of my space. I noticed that she would wait until I stepped out before coming in to service the room, which I really appreciated. Her professionalism and warmth made a real impression on me and made the stay feel comfortable and cared for.

I also ordered breakfast both mornings I was there, and Jordyn was fantastic. She was courteous, friendly, and very respectful. She set everything up nicely and made sure I had everything I needed. It’s the kind of service that feels genuine and welcoming, and it started my mornings on a great note.

The property itself is beautiful. There are plenty of outdoor seating areas where you can relax and enjoy the surroundings. The atmosphere feels open, calm, and well maintained.

reviews.text: Beautiful location in the heart of paradise valley. Stunning hotel and nice well maintained quiet pool areas. We got a cabana and the space and amenities were amazing. reviews.text:
Lots to unpack here. The property itself is a gem. What a great retreat away from the city. Check in was easy and staff was attentive. Let me go category by category on my experiences.

Service team: generally excellent. Our dinner service at the steakhouse was exceptional and the staff there deserve tons of praise. The lobby shop staff was less than friendly - one woman there told several people they were separate from the hotel and couldn't do room charges ("well we could but it would be a pain"), which she said almost with some pride. The only thing she said to me was "we don't allow returns or exchanges" as if I might look like I was going to wear the clothes then return them when I was done. It was weird.

Food all over was excellent, to the pool cafe and the two restaurants we ate at. Breakfast was tiny, way overpriced and basic but that was a small hiccup - but don't expect any good espresso drinks here.

We stayed in a casita and it was a bit disappointing. The shower was super tiny - think airline economy bathroom - yet the giant bathtub took up literally 1/2 the bathroom proper. The shower head and hand sprayer both sprayed at the same time with no means to turn one off. The knob was broken. And, the door leaked with every shower so half our towels went straight to the floor. Our casita had a walk-out to the parking structure only, terrible view. With no kitchen, a micro fridge, no microwave, it felt like a much cheaper room. Bed was nice though!

The real disappointment for me was, there was really no "kid free" zone. There were two hot tubs lined with kids, even late at night. It's less like a resort and more like a kids water park. My towels were taken by others twice in 30 minutes, (once by staff and once by a child).

This place has potential and I wanted to like it. Even at our romantic, $600 dinner at the steakhouse we were surrounded by children! It kind of ruined the experience for us. The adults only pool was in the middle of the chaos and not peaceful at all. We won't be back unless they work to segregate these areas better. I think we learned our lesson.
reviews.author: T Esk

reviews.text: Do not stay here, and whatever you do, do not book a casita. They are like run down college dorm apartments. They moved us to the main tower but it still did not meet what we were expecting. There's another Marriott property at Camelback that has stunning casitas and rooms, highly recommend looking there. They think very highly of themselves here and it's not worth the price.

reviews.text: Rooms very expensive: nearly $1K+ night 12/28-30/2025. Great location. Rooms are solid, though shower is a bit cramped.

reviews.text: Very dated rooms and hotel, broken water pipes lead to no running water/toilets for over 10-hours. We received no notifications or messages as to the water going out and no updates during the day. When we finally waited in line for over an hour at 10pm at night we were moved rooms wjth the promise not to have to move again, until the next day when we were moved again…terrible experience for a lux resort would never go back or recommend. Once moved to the canyon suites we enjoyed ourselves, but would not suggest the main hotel.

The rooms were very large and had a great view of orchid falls we loved sitting outside near the fire place  because of the view. The restaurants had a very good view but there were limited options.

reviews.text:

The room is nice but it is not enjoyable sitting on the balcony since next to the pool in front of the balconies there is a large enclosure of the heating/air-conditioning commercial unit making significant noise.

reviews.text: Gorgeous grounds. Beautiful rooms. Delicious food.

reviews.text:
Marriott elite member here.  Came here for an early Xmas escape.  I didn't book the room but as a Marriott member, this location is not a "luxury" resort as they brand themselves to be.  On our last day, they had a water pipe burst and shut down all the water in the resort.  We couldn't even use a restroom for about 5 hours until they brought porta jons to the front of the hotel to use.  And then the staff offered a "free" bus to another hotel to shower.  My guess is that when Marriott bought this property, they took a significant amount of risk on the infrastructure and a max capacity tested their limits.

On top of the water issues, the rooms are old and dated, adult pool is surrounded by kids pools and, and everything is overpriced just due to the Phoenician name and history of the resort.  If you are a Marriott member I would recommend the W or JW Marriott over this property.

reviews.text:
If I had to sum up the Phoenician in a single sentence, I would say: it seems like a property that was once great, but has significantly lost its luster.

I’ll start with the good. Everyone working at the Phoenician that we interacted with was excellent, both genuinely friendly as well as very helpful and competent. The property itself and the grounds are beautiful, nestled into the foothills of Camelback Mountain. The spa services were fantastic, and the restaurants were very good.

Now here’s the cons. This feels like a resort that has about 300 fewer people working there than it should. For just an example, something simple like a request for ice to our room required nearly an hour wait and a follow up phone call. This doesn’t seem like anyone not doing their job appropriately, but simply that there wasn’t enough people for the requests that were made. For another, at their marketplace, on a weekday, with a conference going on, it seemed like there was only one, very kind, but very stressed out guy working at the counter (making food, coffee, taking orders, etc). This was a frequent experience/thought I had during our stay.

At the pools, what should have been a polished experience, given the location, was lackluster. The pools were freezing cold, to the extent that almost no one except for some brave children were using them. Are their heaters not being maintained? Or turned off to save cost? The pool chairs at this luxury property were mostly basic pool chairs and the tables for drinks were wicker and falling apart. Our server on several days, was very nice, but seemingly was attending to three different levels of pools, meaning we were often waiting for extended periods of time to order another drink, food, or get our tab (not for lack of her effort, to be clear). The pool experience at a luxury property should be a luxury experience, fast service, towel service, heated pools, comfortable chairs. This felt like a pool at a low end all inclusive (without the free drinks).

Finally the rooms. Remember, this is a property that often charges $900+ a night, if not more. We were in the casitas, and upon arriving, the outdoor firepit was out of propane, and our in room phone didn’t work. The temperature control was lackluster, needing to be kept at 65 degrees to maintain a comfortable air temp, and even then the vents was dripping onto the floor (and the covered in dust). Our one experience with in room dining was good, but the pickup took nearly two hours, with the person knocking on our door at nearly 10 PM. At one point in the bathroom we also found a large spider web hanging from the ceiling. Again, at a lower caliber property, all these things are to be expected. At a five star resort in Marriott’s luxury line? This is unacceptable.

All in all, my experience was fine, to pretty good. Obviously all these issues are minor. Unfortunately, because of the cost, these seemingly minor issues leave a poor taste in your mouth. For my money, next time I’ll go with a Ritz Carlton or Four Seasons, which seems to be much more reliable in their attention to detail and understanding real high level service and experience.

Prices are outrageous, and it feels like they’re trying to squeeze every dollar out of you at every step.

Yes, the hotel and pools are nice, but you’ll find similar pools and comfort at much cheaper hotels nearby. Nothing here truly justifies the insane prices except maybe the view, and even that’s not worth paying such an absurd premium for.

Self-parking far from the rooms is $30 a day, faster Wi-Fi costs extra, and you constantly get the sense that everything has an added charge. It’s a beautiful property ruined by greed.

Bottom line: you can easily find a $200–300 hotel in Scottsdale that will give you an equal or even better experience without draining your wallet.

reviews.text:
Where do I even start?! From the moment we arrived, The Phoenician delivered an unforgettable experience of luxury, ease, and pure indulgence. Every single detail... from the breathtaking views of Camelback Mountain to the impeccably designed rooms... made this birthday getaway feel like a true oasis in the desert.

The property itself is immaculate; modern elegance with a classic touch. The grounds are perfectly maintained, the pools are serene and photo-worthy, and the spa? Absolutely divine. I spent hours unwinding at the rooftop spa pool, and I can honestly say I left floating.

But what really made this stay exceptional was the service. Every staff member we encountered was warm, attentive, and genuinely helpful...from valet to concierge to the poolside attendants. They didn’t just meet expectations, they anticipated our needs. One staff member even gave us spot-on recommendations for local restaurants and lounges that ended up being highlights of our trip.

This hotel understands the meaning of true hospitality. Whether you’re celebrating a special occasion or just in need of a luxurious escape, The Phoenician will wrap you in comfort, class, and a kind of care that’s hard to put into words.

I can't wait to return. Consider this my official love letter to The Phoenician.

This is my second time staying here over Labor Day weekend. I returned because the housekeeping, pool staff, and valet team are all wonderful professional, kind, and welcoming. Unfortunately, the front desk experience has once again been very disappointing.

On both visits, there were booking and service issues that I brought to the front desk, and both times I was met with dismissive and unhelpful responses. As someone who has worked in the hotel industry as a Front Office Manager, I know how critical the first impression at the front desk is. If a guest has a problem, it should be an opportunity to turn the situation around whether that’s with an upgrade, a drink voucher, or even just a genuine effort to resolve the issue with care.

The front desk sets the tone for the entire stay, and if that interaction is poor, it overshadows all the positive aspects of the property. For the rates charged here, investing $10–20 in guest recovery when issues arise is a small price to pay for guest satisfaction and loyalty.

Until improvements are made with the front office staff, I would hesitate to recommend this hotel to friends despite the excellent service from the other departments.

reviews.text:
A Beautiful Stay with Room for Improvement

The Phoenician Resort is undeniably stunning, from the breathtaking mountain views near our hotel room to the beautifully landscaped grounds, multiple pool options, and towering palm trees that truly make the resort feel like a desert oasis. However, while the scenery impressed us, several aspects of our stay fell short, especially when compared to other top resorts in the Phoenix area.

Dining & Amenities:
One major concern was the limited dining hours. Most on-site restaurants closed by 5:00 PM, with The Tavern being the only option open until 8:00 PM. As out-of-town guests, this left us with little choice in the evenings aside from room service or ordering out. We expected more flexibility and variety in a luxury resort.

Shops & Pool Experience:
All shops on the property also closed early at 5:00 PM, and pool amenities, including the water slide, music, bar, and even the water fountains, were shut down around the same time. This was disappointing, as the pool is typically a hub of activity and relaxation, especially in the summer.

Children's Activities:
We were especially let down by the Funicians Kids Club, which was never open during our stay. This was a major reason we selected the Phoenician, and our children were incredibly disappointed by its unavailability.

Summer Activities:
We appreciated the advertised “Legendary Summers” theme, but there were no events scheduled during the weekdays only on the weekends. Other Phoenix-area resorts we’ve visited provide daily family-friendly activities all summer long, so the lack of weekday activities was a letdown.

Overall, while the resort is visually impressive and offers a serene setting, we felt the guest experience didn’t fully match the high rating and reputation. With a few key improvements especially around extended hours, family activities, and consistent activites the Phoenician could offer a truly legendary experience to match its branding.

reviews.text:
Date: 06/14/25

Title: “The Best of the Best”

Pros:

* Guarded checkpoint at the main entrance

* a luxurious resort entrance with Camelback Mountain in the backdrop.

* Several accommodation options on site including under ground parking. With a fully functional parking garage.

* I was very surprised how they were able to bring the classic luxury experience into 2025.

* Valet is always available to assist you at the main entrance with all of your transportation needs day or night.

* The main lobby entrance is very grand and opulent with people catering to your every need and fountains I mean the whole nine yards.

* This location offers a true resort experience almost as if you’re away in another country.

* It’s located in one of the best locations in Scottsdale across from Old Town Scottsdale and adjacent to Paradise Valley.

* They have several eating options on site. Such as The Markerplace adjacent to the main lobby which is like a cafe bistro. Across from that is an actual convenience store like shop within the hotel. They have Mowry & Cotton which has a great everyday food menu with class. They also have The Tavern which is like a pub with excellent food options but more casual. They have a restaurant at the pool named Kalio. You can get food also at Thirsty Camel which is the lobby bar that has excellent food options. The crown jewel is J&G steakhouse with excellent service and views of Camelback Mountain. And lastly they have 24/7 room service.

* onsite there are several activities and venues such as the Athletic Center, Tennis Courts, Game Room, Golf Center, Several Pools with a slide, The Phoenician Spa and even a kids center called Funicians Club.

* There are 645 total accommodations: 577 guest rooms and 68 suites. Guest rooms span 600 square feet; suites are twice that size with one or two bedrooms. I stayed in a Grand Deluxe King w/ pool view this trip which was lovely like a mini suite. In the past I have stayed in the large suites which is just as lovely with more space. The rooms have a very classic feel but are still very modern and updated.

* They have the Canyon Suites on-site which is a separate hotel within a hotel. I will review that one at a later date. Although it’s supposed to have a more personalized luxury experience.

* $100 incidental per night and a $50 resort fee per night

* Romantic/Nature Inspired Cactus Garden across from the main lobby entrance.

Cons:

* no house car anymore for everyone except VIP and people staying at the canyon suites. To be honest I’m mentioning this because it was an experience when they did have it. But of course Ubers are readily available.

* there was no trash bin in my bathroom. Just overall there should have been more small trash bins in the room I had.

* The property is very large. There are so many things available to do and see. Although they do provide you with a guide at check in. It would be nice to have property tours if they don’t already have this.

* There were so many shops/food options available on-site that I had no idea about until I literally toured the whole property.

Summary:

This is the place that you stay when you have finally made it in life. Anything you want or need is here on site or close by including the stunning views of Camelback Mountain. If you’re looking for a true resort experience this place provides that and more. I believe my title for this place says it all.

Thumbs Up Or Down: Thumbs Up

Key People:

Devin - Front Desk (a true GEM for the property with his knowledge and skillset with the charisma to match)

Javier - Front Desk (another star I encountered on site. He checked me in and was able to determine exactly the experience I was looking for and he nailed it)

Chad - Bell desk (exceptional service, remembered my name, and made me feel special and valued each time I encountered him)

Dino - Bartender (he may be the best mixologist in Phoenix)

Sydney - Hostess (The Tavern) - very knowledgeable and helpful when explaining the menu and the property.

Let me start by saying: now I understand why this resort isn’t rated higher.

We just wrapped up a week-long trip to Arizona, and unfortunately, The Phoenician—our final stop—left us disappointed. For a property that positions itself as luxury, the experience felt more like a series of hidden fees and lackluster service. From unexpected porter charges to an overall feeling of being nickel-and-dimed, it simply didn’t deliver on the value.

One of the most unsettling parts of our stay was the check-in process. Not only was it disorganized and slow, but the way we were treated compared to other guests was noticeably different. I don’t make assumptions lightly—but the energy and lack of courtesy felt borderline discriminatory. It’s 2025. That should never be part of anyone’s travel experience.

Also worth noting: if you’re a Marriott Bonvoy member—especially with elite status—don’t expect your loyalty to be honored here. The usual recognition and perks seem nonexistent at this property.

We were extremely disappointed with our recent stay at The Phoenician, which unfortunately fell far short of the "luxury resort" experience it promises.

The most shocking part of our visit was discovering a cockroach in our bed, under the covers, in our hotel room. To make matters worse, our room was located directly next to the garbage area—on the third floor—which we believe may explain how the cockroach got in.

The room itself was also outdated and did not reflect the luxurious feel portrayed on the resort’s website, nor the outrages price for what you get. We chose The Phoenician to try something new, even though we've previously had excellent experiences at the Andaz. Sadly, this was a mistake.

When I showed the photo of the cockroach to the receptionist, they visibly jolted in shock—but to their credit, they handled the situation very professionally. They kindly comped our room, which we appreciated, and we immediately checked out and moved to the Andaz - an incredibly inconvenient process that ended up wasting hours of our vacation. Instead of relaxing, we had to pack up, leave, and coordinate a new stay at another resort.. Not only was The Andaz resort more affordable(which I still cant comprehend), our experience at the Andaz was once again outstanding and felt like we were genuienly taken care of—just as we remembered.

What struck us as particularly odd was that, despite the seriousness of the issue, no one from the management team came out to apologize. The receptionist went to speak with them and explained the situation, yet there was no follow-up or acknowledgment from management. That lack of accountability was disappointing.

In summary, The Phoenician felt more like a Motel 6 than a high-end resort. While the front desk staff did their job well, the overall experience was unacceptable. We won’t be returning and strongly recommend the Andaz resort instead—it’s truly a dream resort and everything we were looking for.

Disappointed by Outdated Rooms and Lack of Upkeep – Far from a 5-Star Experience

As a frequent luxury traveler and hospitality reviewer, I had high expectations for The Phoenician given its longstanding reputation as one of Arizona’s premier resorts. While the natural setting of the property is undeniably beautiful, the overall experience unfortunately fell short of what one would expect from a resort commanding $900–$1,000 per night.

To begin with, I want to commend the staff, who were gracious and clearly made efforts to ensure our stay was as pleasant as possible. Their professionalism and willingness to assist did not go unnoticed. However, service alone cannot compensate for the physical condition of the accommodations, which were frankly quite disappointing.

The guest rooms are in serious need of renovation. The design and furnishings felt dated, but more concerning were the cleanliness and maintenance issues. Black mold was visible in the showers, vents were caked with dust, and we encountered multiple bugs in the room—issues that are unacceptable at any level of hospitality, let alone a luxury property. HVAC systems appeared neglected, contributing to poor air quality and discomfort.

At its current state, the rooms reflect the experience of a mid-tier hotel priced at $200 per night—not a luxury resort nearing four figures. Unless there is a significant and comprehensive overhaul of the rooms and facilities, I cannot in good faith recommend The Phoenician as a 5-star destination. I will not be returning until the resort undergoes a transformation that aligns its offerings with its pricing and reputation.

Attention any families with young kids wanting to come here:
The rooms are not luxury at all and disgusting. The carpet is from 30 years ago and the rooms haven’t been updated probably since. The customer service is abysmal. I asked a server for a glass so I can have some juice at the buffet I was paying for and he said I should go back to my table and get it myself…. The servers at the pool were rude too and don’t act like an even 3 star resort.

The food on property is also horrendous. All claiming to be high end and luxury but it is anything but. Room service, terrible. The pool food is decent but it takes an hour to receive it. There’s no fast casual place to pick up food for little kids. We had to drive off property most days.

The pool area was also atrocious. There barely were any attendants helping with towels, you have to hunt them down. No one cleans up, there’s trash everywhere and all of the chairs are gross and stained. There was also trash all over the resort.

They also don’t comp parking if you are staying at the resort, which just feels like another way they can squeeze every last dollar from you.

For the amount of money we are spending here it’s a huge disappointment. Next time I’ll stay at a four seasons or the ritz for these prices.

Oh and a sandwich at their “marketplace” was $20 for one! Highway robbery!

Also worth noting we are lifetime gold members and they didn’t do anything for us either.

reviews.text:
We came The Phoenician for the 3rd time for Spring Break. Full disclosure: it was a last minute trip and we selected the most affordable room with two queen beds but it was still $850+ per night. We had had great experiences in our past two trips so it seemed like a safe bet. Initially I noticed the hall on the walk to our room smelled faintly of urine - like the floor of an old pub - but the room seemed fine so I let it go. On day two of our trip we noticed an intense plumbing/sewage smell outside our room and in parts of our room. We left and came back and the smell was still there. I called the front desk and they assured me they’d send an engineer immediately. Someone walking down the hall literally said “it smells like poop.” Forty five minutes later no one showed and I waited on hold for the front desk for 10 minutes before walking down to discuss in person. I explained the situation and they agreed to move us to a casita that “I would love.” As we were packing up the room the engineer showed up with a cleaning spray. Not a chance that was going to be sufficient. We got to the casita and the room was nice but had double beds instead of queens which doesn’t work for a family of four. We were moved again to a room with two queens. This room had a concrete wall outside the tiny patio. Literally a wall. After going back to the front desk AGAIN I was advised they were at very high capacity and options were slim. I get that they can’t change that. We ended up in a 4th room that is dark and down at the farthest end of the hotel. The recording while I was on hold with the front desk repeated that this Luxury Collection is for the discerning traveler. We are long time Marriott members with Titanium Elite status. I understand that the staff could not magic me a better room but I got the continued feeling that staff was doing whatever was going to move me along the fastest. There was a lack of care and more a ticking of the box of ‘problem technically handled.’ That’s not a luxury approach. This is three star treatment at five star prices. I was not treated as a discerning traveler. This ruined my day. Ruined my dinner plans. Ruined my trip. Will not return. Would not recommend.

Other notable mentions: Pool staff was very good and friendly but stretched too thin. Shout out to Gennaro. Bryan in bell service was wonderful. Gloria at Mowry + Cotton was amazing.

We recently hosted a conference for 70 guests at The Phoenician, and I can say with complete confidence that it was an unforgettable experience. What truly made our event exceptional, however, was the incredible staff. Their attention to detail, professionalism, and warm hospitality made every step of the process seamless and enjoyable. It’s clear that the team at The Phoenician is dedicated to providing an outstanding experience, and they certainly delivered.

Not only was the venue beautiful, but the service was flawless. The event spaces were well-equipped and thoughtfully arranged, and the catering and amenities were outstanding. Our guests had nothing but praise for every aspect of the event.

We’re so grateful to The Phoenician for making our conference an absolute success. It’s rare to work with a team that combines exceptional service with such a breathtaking location. We look forward to returning and highly recommend The Phoenician to anyone seeking a perfect venue for their event!

Day before arriving, (12/30) I called to confirm my stay as I had booked with AmEx. Was told by Brad the reservation was cancelled. Spent over an hour on the phone with AmEx to learn Marriott didn’t have permission to cancel AND had not notified myself or AmEx. Brad was seemingly helpful, but suggested to me to “re-book” which would have been at a higher rate. I refused and AmEx resolved that issue.
Arrived the next day (12/31) at 130 and checked in. At 4 pm, the advertised checkin time,  my room wasn’t ready. At 4:35 I went to the front desk and was told the room wasn’t ready, BUT if I wanted to move to a lower level floor they could check me in. One person, who I won’t mention by name, for fear of him being punished for his honesty, told me point blank it was a lesser room than I had booked and paid for and not to move. I then asked to speak with Brad, who acted the day before as if he was in a position of authority. Brad told me the room wasn’t a downgrade and if I “really wanted to check-in then I should just take the room that was available.” No, thank you and you are dishonest. When I asked for my 5 pm dinner reservation to be moved, I was questioned why that would be necessary. Let’s see, it’s 440, I’ve been traveling, need to change and YOU still don’t have me in a room. Reluctantly, Brad/Bryce called and moved the reservation to later.
From there we had the worst service. Waited for service EVERY single time at Mowry & Cotton. Ordered hot tea with drinks, it came out 20+ minutes later. Ordered more cream cheese for a bagel, it never was brought. Plates stacked everywhere outside from the breakfast buffet, including on our table inside, and no server to clear or clean them up for 30+ minutes. Birds flying everywhere and eating off plates because it was a mess anytime we dined outside. Felt like we were dining in a scene from the Birds movie! The bird man did what he could to keep the birds away, but nothing helps when dirty dishes are left sitting for lengthy periods!
On 1/3 the server outside at Thirsty Camel was painfully slow. Ended up going inside to get more drinks where she proceeded to make a comment about us not waiting. We waited and waited AND we were the only people outside. Glasses and plates stacked outside and not cleaned up for over an hour while we sat there. We ended up moving all the glasses to the other side of the fire pit to get them out of our way.
Amanda, at the pool, was great. She was kind, prompt. She deserves a raise.
I stayed at Phoenician Suites years ago and the service was impeccable. I convinced my boyfriend and his kids to join us this trip and was embarrassed I recommended this hotel.
I can unequivocally say the service was not 5 star, in most cases it was barely a 2. There is ZERO reason to return and pay the prices being charged and receive terrible service. Brad is in serious need of being trained!
Calling yourself a 5 star resort is like Carnival claiming to be a 5 star cruise ship. I don’t cruise, but if I was, it wouldn’t be on Carnival. I do enjoy 5 star resorts, but NOT this one anymore. Sadly.

The Phoenician, a Luxury Collection Resort in Scottsdale, offers an enjoyable and upscale experience overall. The facilities are impressive, with a beautifully maintained spa and a gym that is top-notch. The on-site restaurants are well-kept, providing a pleasant dining atmosphere.

We stayed in the casitas, which are townhouse-style accommodations located around the main hotel building. The convenience of parking right outside the unit was a great perk. However, the room itself felt a bit small, and the building seemed dated, which detracted slightly from the otherwise luxurious experience.

The breakfast for Marriott elite members is only a yogurt parfait and a coffee.  You can get other items on their menu for extra fee.  So it’s very easy to pay $50 to $80 to get what you want.  We just came from a JW Marriott that had an amazing breakfast for its members.  I highly recommend they improve that.  The main reason we picked this hotel was it’s a part of Marriott.

While the resort is clearly making efforts to maintain its charm, some areas could benefit from further updates to match the high standards associated with its reputation. Nevertheless, The Phoenician remains a good choice for a relaxing getaway in Scottsdale, especially if you value amenities and serene surroundings.

reviews.text:
At the Phoenician Resort, member of the Marriott Luxury Collection, the authentic Mother-of-Pearl tiles were imported from Italy for $1 million to create the illustrious resort centerpiece known as the “Mother of Pearl” serenity pool. The tiles were hand-laid at the bottom of the pool to create a glistening, iridescent sanctuary – much like the inside of a sea shell.

Over the last 32 years, I have visited this pool seven times. It was always for adults only, but changed somewhere between our visits in 2016 and 2021. We met people from all over the world that reserved their cabanas a year in advance for the next year. It was quiet, beautiful, serene and spiritual.

Under any circumstance, when asked to imagine my happy place, I always imagine going underwater in the beautiful Mother of Pearl pool. Other guests have confirmed the serenity in the pool is like a sense of healing or spirituality.

In my home, you will find multiple pictures of the Mother of Pearl pool and the cabana looking towards Camelback Mountain, and also from the inside of the cabana across the Mother of Pearl pool. Last time I was here, I even took a video just walking through the pool with the sun shimmering on the Mother of Pearl tiles. I’ve played this video many times in anxious situations.

I am sad to say it has greatly changed. It is filled with Styrofoam noodles and children screaming at the top of their lungs and little babies crying. It has become the kiddie pool! Parents aren’t paying attention to the children. People not paying for the reserved cabana area are using my reserved towels. There is no pool etiquette; no etiquette in general. The younger attendants have no control.

Times have certainly changed, and I believe that The Phoenician is not the worthy of the mark as Luxury Collection it once was, but it is more serving of the mass market.  So be careful if you are expecting something more exclusive. It is not what it was. Our first two nights we did not receive turn down service nor was our room cleaned before 6:00 PM. The managers on duty tried to correct the situation however we shouldn’t have to ask to have the room cleaned if we are paying an extraordinary amount a night and expect a level of service as Platinum members from the Marriott Luxury Collection. Maybe we’re paying the full price rack rate and others got a discount on Priceline? I never thought to look. So, my question is do we need to go to the level of Ritz Carlton to get what we expect? We are.

reviews.text:
I recently stayed at The Phoenician in Scottsdale with my wife and kids, and after reading all the glowing reviews, I just don’t understand the hype. It was fine, but I wouldn’t call it luxury by any means, nor exceptional, especially considering the price or the points required for a stay here. As a Gold Elite member with years of travel experience, I’ve come to recognize top-notch service and value, but this resort falls short in nearly every category.

First impressions matter, and our check-in experience wasn’t great. We didn’t feel welcomed or even like we were at a luxury resort. The staff member who checked us in barely explained anything about the property—just handed me a map and a booklet and sent us on our way.
The main pool area was closed for maintenance, and the kids' splash park wasn’t working when we tried to use it—not once, but twice. The only other pool available for kids was cold! Honestly, no one else was in it because it felt unheated, and after talking to a few guests, they agreed it was too cold. We also didn’t see any pool attendants around to ask about life jackets or pool toys, or anything that might make the experience better if the pool was heated.

The kids' club or play area was also closed on Monday, so there was literally nothing for our kids to do for the first couple of days of our stay. Fortunately, we had a larger unit with a hot tub and a golf cart to get around, which helped salvage the experience—without that, there wouldn’t have been much to do.

Speaking of the hot tub, not good. After using it on Sunday, the next day all of us had rashes or skin breakouts. We suspect it was from the excessive chlorine, as there was an unusually thick layer of foam and bubbles in the tub. Our 5-year-old, 1.5-year-old, and both adults all had reactions.

Room 7704 itself was disappointing, especially for the price and points required. It’s showing its age—there were missing pieces of flooring near the dining table (my wife actually hurt her toe), cracks and dents in the walls, and the doors don’t close properly. The whole place just felt a bit run-down. I certainly wouldn’t pay thousands to stay here.

The wifi also didn’t work for our entire stay which wasn’t ideal at all. I had a couple of meetings Monday and no wifi.  Costing me money to use data. We called down to have someone come up and check it out Sunday but nobody came for almost 2 hours. Called back to inform them nobody came by, kids had to go to sleep. They were going to update the ticket and have someone come by Monday. Nobody came, no follow up, nothing. Just terrible service.

We also ordered food from the Tavern one night, and it was mediocre at best—not worth the price at all. Save your money and eat elsewhere.

As a Gold Elite member, I expected better treatment, especially with pools being closed and limited activities for kids on certain days of the week. We were hoping for an upgrade to a unit with a pool, which is supposed to happen as a gold elite member (enhanced room upgrade benefit) but despite some of the other residences being vacant both nights, they didn’t offer us anything. They were more focused on charging extra for upgrades than making sure we had a better experience, even though we were loyal members with kids and limited options at the resort.

Honestly, I regret spending 240,000 points to stay here. This resort was a major disappointment overall, and I’ll definitely be looking elsewhere next time. It was a huge waste of both time and points.

I encourage others looking to spend their hard earned dollars or points to look elsewhere.

For those of you who love this place, glad you enjoyed it and had a better experience. I know it’s hard to please everyone and it’ll rarely happen but we felt overall, it simply underwhelming and not worth it.

My husband and I were celebrating our 30th anniversary at The Phoenician. We arrived and were greeted warmly by the welcoming staff. Property was absolutely beautiful and in keeping with the Five Star rating! We checked into our room
and while we were settling in we could hear babies crying loudly from adjacent walls in our suite? We waited patiently as we are parents and understand that dealing with toddlers can be challenging. However, it went on all night. Finally stopping from 4AM-7AM when we were able to rest. The next day we awoke and hubby went to golf. I went to the pool which was beautiful. We proceeded to have a lovely afternoon adventuring to the local shops and heading to the gym. That evening we went to the fabulous steak restaurant and had a fabulous meal at J&G. Only return back to the room to screaming of adjacent toddler. I called the front desk and spoke with Ana who promised to have the manager reach out to me the next day to have us moved to another room. The next day no one reached out to us so I left another message. Still no one followed up. We spent four nights and five days listening to babies scream all night long. What was to be a fabulous anniversary celebration turned into a romper room level of unexpected disappointment. We loved our meals. Loved the amenities. reviews.text:
My husband and I just enjoyed 4 nights at the resort. Service was amazing. Javier at guest registration was very kind and accommodating. His service set the tone.

We had lunch at Maury & Cotton as soon as we arrived. The food was great and the staff was amazing. We arrived after their lunch hour which technically should only be a very limited bar menu but the manager brought us the regular menu proactively, we didn’t even ask. We were both so hungry that we would have made anything work. It was a great gesture and indication that customer service is their number one priority.

We rented cabana’s at the adult only pool which was awesome. They included the cabana with seating within, 4 lounge chairs by the pool, as well as a patio table with seating for 4. The rental could comfortably accommodate 6-8 people as long as everyone doesn’t need to be on a lounge at the same time. there were lots of other perks like snacks, several treats throughout the day, sunscreen, etc. Christine and Raymond were our attendants and both were superb, really excellent service and nice people.

We spent a day at the spa which we were both very impressed with. I had my massage with Tomas. For someone who frequently gets massages, this was one of the best by far. He was very professional and had a strong yet not unpleasant technique to tackle the knots in my back. After our services we spent the day at the private spa rooftop pool. Lee was our attendant poolside and again her service was amazing.

Our only meh feedback was the room. It was clean and everything you would expect but there was nothing exceptional about it. We were both underwhelmed but will say that the property overall made up for it.

Overall we highly recommend The Phoenician and look forward to our next stay!

reviews.text:
My stay at The Phoenician was truly exceptional. From the moment I arrived, I was welcomed with outstanding service and attention to detail. The resort’s stunning location, nestled at the base of Camelback Mountain, provided breathtaking views and a tranquil atmosphere that made my stay unforgettable.

The accommodations were pure luxury—elegantly designed with spacious rooms, plush bedding, and a well-appointed bathroom. The attention to detail, from the nightly turndown service to the luxurious amenities, exceeded my expectations.

The resort’s amenities are top-notch. I especially enjoyed the pool area, which offered an oasis-like experience with its multiple pools, cabanas, and excellent poolside service. The golf course is beautifully maintained, and for spa enthusiasts, The Phoenician Spa is a must-visit, offering a range of treatments in a peaceful, rejuvenating setting.

Dining at The Phoenician was a highlight. The fine dining options, including Mowry & Cotton and J&G Steakhouse, served exquisite dishes with impeccable service. Every meal was a delight, with a wide variety of options for every palate.

If I had to mention one small downside, it would be that the property is quite expansive, so walking between amenities can take some time. However, the beautiful surroundings and helpful staff more than made up for this.

Overall, The Phoenician exceeded all expectations and provided a perfect blend of luxury, comfort, and top-tier service. I highly recommend this resort for anyone seeking a high-end, relaxing getaway.

reviews.text:
I want to start off with the pros of my experience staying with them for labor day week;
Pros- Large rooms, beautiful clean amenities, free parking, pools allowed night swims, 18+ areas. Housekeeping was the most professional. Pool side service amazing.

**Cons:** DO NOT CHARGE TO THE ROOM. On the first day of our stay, we reserved a poolside cabana and had an excellent experience. However, when it was time to pay, the server casually mentioned, "on the room," and we agreed. Unfortunately, this led to a pending charge of $2,600 on our account on top of the cabana charge and incidentals. The resort's billing system pulls pending money based on what you've charged to the room, so they imagine what you "plan" to spend which is both confusing and problematic. We’ve stayed at numerous resorts and have never encountered such a practice. When we raised this issue with the staff, we were simply told we shouldn’t have put it on the room, as if we had been informed otherwise. It’s unacceptable for a system to lock up funds without prior notice, and we couldn’t access the money until we checked out three days later. Our bank has informed us that the funds may remain inaccessible for 7-14 more days.

Additionally, the concierge service was disappointing. The two middle-aged women working in that department were unkind. At one point, we were turned away after being directed to them by the front desk. One concierge then proceeded to sit on the floor in the center of the lobby, talking loudly to a child in an unprofessional manner until her co-worker helped her up off the floor. This behavior was unprofessional and unexpected at such a "highly established" location. Everyone was uneasy who witnessed it. The staff’s demeanor needs significant improvement and clearly needs some more proper training.

A great place to stay - especially for Bonvoy members to either rack up or use points. The  resort is beautiful and impeccably maintained outside. Considerations...

Rooms: Zero complaints. I would opt for an outside building with private patio.

Gym: Excellent and well maintained equipment. Lots of treadmills and cardio machines. Free weights - dumbbells and kettlebells. Cable and smith machine. Rowing machine too! Spacious with bottled water and lots of towels. You don't have to compromise your workout on the road.

Bar: Huge bar area in main building. Great atmosphere and friendly bartenders.

Pools: Multiple. Including an adult only pool if you're not there to deal with kids. Pool area has plenty of umbrellas, lounge chairs, cabanas.

Food: Dinner at The Tavern onsite restaurant was excellent. Recommend the Pull Apart Pretzel, Stone Fruit & Arugula salad.

Overall: Great place for business stay and also a couples getaway. Can't speak to the golf course. The staff was top notch from arrival through checkout.

reviews.text: This was our third year in a row visiting this destination resort and it continues to exceed expectations. Location: Considering the fact The Phoenician Resort is located in the booming metropolis of Phoenix/Scottsdale, its proximity to Camelback mountain is one redeeming factor that makes the venue even more spectacular. Service: 10 stars. Service has always been excellent, but this year, Bryce (our check-in agent at the front desk) set the bar even higher. First, he remembered our request made 3 days earlier by phone when we asked if our Casita included a Nespresso machine. (He explained the adjacent Canyon Suites have Nespresso machines, but the Casitas do not). No worries as we could bring our travel-Nespresso machine for this 4-day trip. Yet he surprised us with a welcome card, anniversary greeting and stated, "Hey since we couldn't upgrade you to the Canyon Suites, we decided to bring a little of the Canyon suites to your Casita and included the Nespresso song on our welcome card."  Now that's a concierge-level of service if I have ever seen one. The Casita's in their own right are fabulous, spacious and first class. 3 different swimming pools, a great waterslide and 4-5 restaurants on-site mean you don't need to go anywhere off property. The fitness facility is nothing short of fabulous. The Phoenician is highly recommended and a destination you won't soon forget.

The pool was gorgeous and sparkling even during the busiest hours — there was also plenty of space to spread out and relax at all the recreational areas, even during high occupancy times.

reviews.text: This place has been around forever, but they have somehow kept it impeccably updated. reviews.text:
This has been hands down the best place I have ever stayed. Everyone I encountered on the staff was polite, friendly and exceptionally professional.
The golf course is immaculate!
Today while walking around the cactus garden out back, I stumbled upon an old golf path. It appears there used to be more holes on the course.  Anyway, there were some old steps leading up to old at boxes. The views at night were spectacular.
It’s super easy to access also.
Once you reach the cactus garden entrances, use the left entrance. There is a statue of a woman holding a bowl. Off to the right of the bench behind her is a palo verde tree. The old cart path is right there. The path is also accessible by entering the garden and heading right. You will eventually see the old cart path from here too.
From either way, take a left until you come to some stairs. Thats it!

reviews.text: This place is hands down not a luxury experience.  For the price go stay at the Biltmore or one of the other amazing resorts in the area.  I have traveled the world and stayed in luxury hotels and this place was rundown, awful service.  The "casitas" remind me of a motel 6.  Construction was going on all around.  The place was being rented for some one year old childs' birthday party and it took over the other guest's experience.  When we arrived we had noon check in on our Marriott Bonvoy app and our room wasn't ready and the manager instead of accommodating proceeded to argue with us.  Told us he could only guarantee our room by 4pm so we came back and 4pm and it still wasn't ready for another half hour.  We had to INSIST on a credit.  It was not offered despite the guarantee and our wait.  Then at the conclusion of the visit my dress was stolen (probably by housekeeping) and they have now put me in touch with their insurer who will not call me back or answer.  One bright spot the spa (which is owned by a separate entity) and DryBar are amazing.  But come enjoy them without staying there.

reviews.text:
Visited in 2023 for a week long family vacation with my husband and young son. We had very high expectations given the luxury marketing and at the end of the day, they missed the mark.

Pros: beautiful property, amazing pools and splash pad, fun amenities on site, including golf! Free kids meals at some restaurants.

Cons: Poor customer service at the front desk. They downgraded our room, after we paid for an upgrade. They also didn't tell us anything about the resort so we had to figure out the amenities on our own. Our room was not well maintained (dirty carpet, rusty railing, chipped flooring, etc) and trash sat outside our room for extended periods of time in the heat.

Overall it's not a 5 star resort, due to lack of customer service and maintenance. BUT if you come in with lower expectations you will probably love this place!

reviews.text:
The property is beautiful. The rooms are not. At least, mine was not. Broken fixtures. Holes in the wall. Paint splatters on the floors. Light fixtures from 30 years ago (fluorescent tubes that hum). Clogged sinks. Stains in the carpet. Old (pre smart tv) tech. One of the sets of drapes were stuck and wouldn’t open.

Other little things like the tons of construction everywhere and the fact that I tried the basketball courts and the basketballs were all tore up all added up to an experience that was just not on par.

Look at my review history and you’ll see that I don’t leave a ton of negative reviews.

It wasn’t “bad” by all hotel standards, but by $1800/night standards, it’s totally unacceptable.

If they remodeled it, then it absolutely could be worth the rate.

As it stands, there is no chance I would recommend the hotel if you want to have an upscale experience.

The resort has potential, but either I was in the lowest quality room on the property (the “executive suite”), or the standards for the rooms themselves are super low for any Marriott.

To be fair, I didn’t pay for it (it was paid for by someone else) - but I have spent a lot of time in a lot of Marriott hotels.

reviews.text:
Stayed here for the long weekend with my husband and 11 month old baby. The location and overall hotel were beautiful but the service left a lot to be desired. On the reservation we listed a need for a crib, my husband called twice prior to the reservation date and on the morning of, and when I checked in I requested a crib. I got to the room needing to put my overtired baby down for a nap. I proceeded to wait *two* more hours (involving two more phone calls) for a crib to arrive; by this point my baby was miserable and it took another hour to get him down for a nap.

We self parked, on the second day, we realized the A elevator in the parking garage lobby was broken. Their elevator system won’t let you summon a different elevator. So, we had to bring our baby in a stroller on the escalator. Imagine if someone in a wheelchair had needed to get upstairs (I’m fairly certain this was an ADA violation). If you’re going to get that kind of elevator system, you better make sure it works.

We needed another comforter; 6 hours later it wasn’t there. The TV chromecast function didn't work. The Parking Garage didn’t work with the room keys.

Overall, this was a disappointing visit. Lovely area and hotel from the outside, but I’ve gotten better, more attentive service at a Best Western.

This place probably was 5 star forty years ago. But now it’s old, outdated and worn out. From the scary dirty parking garage to the run down lobby areas, it looks rough. (See photos) Broken floor tiles, cracked glass doors, finishes from decades ago. I’ve stayed at actual 5 star resorts and this is NOT. It looks like they have unable to afford maintenance and updates for many years. Which is surprising considering their insane rates!

Anyways our stay was booked with a discounted rate. So they stuck us in a room with the view literally being a stucco wall directly outside of the window lol! We could see ac thin slice of the sky above the wall. It was really unbelievable. We started laughing when we opened the shades. It’s not really the kind of room anyone should pay money for. It would make a good storage room. Oh and the bathroom has industrial T-bar ceiling. Like the kind at the DMV. This is the mentality of the owners. And that’s who has decided not to maintain the property for decades.

There are so many nice new modern resorts. Don’t waste your time at this run down dinosaur lol

This review has nothing to do with the room quality or amenities or facilities, those are all quite nice and frankly should be for the nightly rate you are paying. This review ties directly to the staff and their lack of care for their guests.

We were there for a weekend with family and friends attending a wedding. On the day of the wedding my wife went to the pool for one hour by herself. She got her towels and set her things down on a chair. She then received a phone call that she took and spoke for 15 minutes next to the pool with her back turned to the chair. At this time someone grabbed all of her things including her purse and sandals. This pool probably had 20 guests at the pool at this time, not a lot of activity. All the staff had the same lethargic response, “I am sorry mam, there is nothing we can do.”

Now let me be crystal clear, we are not ascribing blame directly to the hotel. They certainly cannot be responsible for all guests' belongings at all times and my wife made a costly error in judgment, although an unconscious one, she never should have turned her back to her items.

We immediately shut down credit cards but saw that the culprit already tried to charge $1,500 at Neiman Marcus just down the street so now we had validation that this was no accident or misplaced items. One gentleman who worked at the front desk (I wish I had his name) even had the nerve to tell us, “Things get stolen from the pool all the time” - If that statement is true, maybe an examination of security protocols might be a priority.

Rather than attend our wedding we spent the reception filling out a police report. We knew the chances of recovery were slim and the financial loss was significant (>$500) but not catastrophic. The point is there is an absolute dearth of security at this resort. I can’t list all the shortcomings but here are a few: There are no cameras anywhere on the three pool decks (at least that is what we were told), All gates to the pools remain wide open at all times. I have stayed at resorts who charge half as much as the phonecian and they still require a room key to access the pools. The parking lot entry attendant showed no enforcement as far as which cars were allowed on property.

Here is the kicker. 7 hours after the purse was first stolen another charge was attempted on our canceled credit card BACK ON THE PHOENICIAN property. We thought this was our chance, how many establishments are even open at 10 PM to accept payment on the property? We alerted hotel management immediately and again the blank stares, the nonchalance, complete and utter deflection, “I am sorry, we can’t track that.” How easy would it have been upon our initial claim to tell their staff “If you run a credit card that is denied then alert security immediately.” With today’s tech and ubiquitous communication that is such an easy catch. You would think at $700/night there might be a modicum of effort or assistance for their guests.

Moral of the Story: Don’t take anything valuable to the pool and Don’t rely on the staff. Their customer service extends as far as reading a script, over and over again. They are sorry, but there is nothing they can do, ahem, willing to do.

(11/15 Follow up to Mr. Fredricks response)
With all due respect Ben, I find it a bit disingenuous to be told I am getting a “response from the business owner” when in reality it is a room operations manager who has been in the workforce for just over six years. I don’t mean to slight you directly Ben, you could be highly proficient at your role and I know this lack of attention to our case is not orchestrated by you. The frustration is with your bosses who are merely applying damage control. It is a strategy as old as time, deflect and neglect. Placate the upset client with feckless apologies in hopes they just go away. You allude to hints of action, “steps are being taken“ . . .

Please feel free to contact us with what exactly these are. We accept your “sincere apologies” but six weeks later, we are awaiting to see what these might be.

I was invited to a private cocktail hour by the sponsor of the conference I am attending. I am a black woman and I arrived with my colleagues who are black and Hispanic. We arrived to the happy hour and spoke to the host. We mingled and said hello to a few attendees. One we sat down and looked over the menu, a waitress came over to take our order. She asked me for my card to start a tab. I thought this was odd because it was a private cocktail event and the host was paying for everything. I gave her my card. I checked in with another attendee and asked if we were paying for our drinks and food. They told me no. When the waitress returned I told her that I was a part of the private event and she said "Oh, someone told me that you all snuck into the back of this event and you're not with them." She politely returned my card, however,  that doesn't change the racial bias that I experienced at the hands of this hotel.

Before taking our initial order she could've asked if we were a part of private event. She could've asked the host. Yet, instead she chose to believe something the "someone" told her. These are microagressions. There was a lack of respect for me because if it was a private event and I want not meant to be in that area, she could've asked me to move. This is how racism persists because two black people and a Hispanic person look like they don't belong at an upscale event at a luxury hotel. My night was soured and my experience at this hotel event as an invited guest was ruined.
