reviews.text:
Imposantes Haus aus den 80igern, das seinen Special Touch noch nicht verloren hat. Das Hotel ist eine Destinationen für sich.

Anreise: In Scottsdale gelegen ist es circa 30 Minuten vom Flughafen. Circa 10 Minuten mit dem Auto zur Fashion Square Mall und zu Old Town Scottsdale Imposante (nicht kontrollierte) Einfahrt, die entlang der Ferienwohnungen und am Golfplatz und am Fitnesskomplex vorbei dann letztendlich im eigentlichen Hotel mündet.

Auf dem Weg zum Hotel passiert man die Canyon Suites. Eigenes Gebäude mit eigenen Empfang und eigenem Pool, etwas teurer. Wir hatten uns dort die Räumlichkeiten zeigen lassen, hatten aber nicht den Eindruck, dass sich der Aufpreis tatsächlich in der Qualität der Räumlichkeiten widerspiegelt, da man im eigentlichen Hotel ohnehin schon auf extrem hohen Niveau ist.
Allerdings ist bei den Canyon Suites (es gibt dort auch „normale“ Zimmer) das Frühstück bereits inbegriffen. Die Poollandschaft des Haupthauses kann man natürlich mit benutzen.

Check In: imposante Vorfahrt mit regionaler Kunst, gespickt. Freundliche Begrüßung durch die Valets, die sofort das Gepäck Aufnahmen und es Richtung Lobby brachten. Check In verlief freundlich und reibungslos. Leider keine kleine Aufmerksamkeit für Kinder. Karte als Überblick wurde ausgehändigt. Guter Concierge Desk.

Die Lobby selbst wird von großen Panoramafenstern und mittiger Bar bestimmt. Lebhafte Lobby zum verweilen.

Zimmer: Zimmer über vier Etagen. Lobby selbst ist im 3. OG. Erst ab Deluxe Pool View hat man einen wirklich schönen Blick. Ansonsten gehen die Zimmer Richtung Hotel - Vorfahrt oder Richtung Berge.

Sehr große Zimmer, mit Sitzecke und großem bestuhlten Balkon. Nicht mehr ganz taufrisch, gut funktionierende Klimaanlage, Kaffeemaschine mit Pads, großes Bad, mit separater Dusche und Badewanne. Viele Ablagemöglichkeiten gut beleuchtet.

Pools/Spa/Fitness: wirklich schöne Pool Landschaft über drei Stufen. Davon ein Pool, nur für Erwachsene; sehr angenehme Wasser Temperaturen. Ausreichend Liegen mit Sonnenschirmen. Weiche Auflagen. Schnelle Wasserrutsche für die Kids + Splash Pad. Sehr großzügig gestaltet. Hinter den Pool befindet sich dann das  separates Spa Gebäude und dahinter der Golfclub.
Fitnessclub für ein Hotel auf Weltklasse Niveau. 24 Stunden. Alles neu!

Für Kids: wie gesagt, große Poollandschaft und Wasserrutsche ist ein Highlight für alle Kids. Zudem gibt es einen großen, mit zahlreichen Videospielen ausgestatteten Game Room unterhalb des Fitness Centers.

Auch wird ein KidsClub angeboten. Allerdings wirkt dieser wenig ansprechen und die Aktivitäten kosten zusätzlich und sind limitiert. Das ginge bei solch ein Luxusadresse sicherlich besser .

Essen: tolles Fleisch im Steakhouse J&G im Obergeschoss. Ansonsten gibt es noch einen Coffee Shop mit gutem Frühstück und frischen Lunch. Lobby mit Snacks. Das Restaurant im Golfclub haben wir nicht besucht. Das Gartenrestaurant war leider geschlossen Mowry&Cotton.

Personal: besonders gut bei Valet und Concierge. Front Desk, mal so mal so. Housekeeping top! Restaurants: das geht besser - J&G unorganisiert.

Fazit: beeindruckendes Luxus-Haus mit toller Poollandschaft und exzellentem Fitness Club. Zimmer könnten einen Refresh vertragen. Personal mal so mal so. Bei Kindern könnte man sich etwas mehr Mühe geben.

I honestly was disappointed with the fact that this resort was 5 stars and was not even comparable to the Hilton Resorts and Hotels I’ve stayed at. I was not impressed with the service and also the restaurants. The resort seemed a bit ran down and needs to be updated. For the price that was paid, it was disappointing. The front desk staff was rude and cold. The pool staff I can honestly say we’re more warm and welcoming. Also the housekeeping staff is amazing. But front desk staff especially during 2nd shift is unbearable. I try to be very understanding and nice as possible. Especially because this Arizona heat is  out of this world, but the service for the front staff for amenities was super slow. Asked for some toothbrushes around 8pm and didn’t get them until around midnight… by that time we all fell asleep and was not going to answer the door. It was a bit rude. Then came the day I ordered doordash and the dasher ends up sending it to the front desk. Told me it would be a $5 charge which is understandable to deliver it to my casita. Did not get my food until two phone calls and a whole hour later. Both times I called the front desk rep was cold and hung up after she told me she was going to send it. I ended up telling her to throw it away as I didn’t have a way to reheat my food. She rudely told me she will send it again and hung up. Then when it was delivered, no one ever knocked on the door. Got a call from the front desk that it was delivered and she hung up again rudely. Just providing some feedback as I usually don’t stay at Marriot properties but was excited that I was invited on vacation with my friends to this “amazing resort”. I say don’t waste your money. This pregnant woman aka me was not happy what so ever. I will make sure I stay at the Waldorf or the W next time when I visit myself.

reviews.text: I recently stayed the phoenician for a business trip. I have traveled to Arizona almost every year of my life and I have always wanted to stay at the phoenician. Overall, I was happy with my stay. I will start off with the bad. The shower pressure was very high and although the shower got hot, the pressure sometimes made it feel like you were getting hosed down. It was fine to get clean, but it was not a very relaxing shower. Also, there were so many bugs in the room. I was not in the room much because of work, I saw grasshoppers in my room on 4 different times. I killed 2 of them so there were at least 3 grasshoppers in my room possibly more. It did make my stay slightly uncomfortable. I told the front desk, but they said there was nothing they could do. I was able to deal with it for my stay but I would not have wanted to spend another night in that room because of the bugs.  For the good, the bathroom was huge with a nice tub The gym was nice and the hotel has excellent service from the valet, to housekeeping and front desk. Overall, I my experience was a 3 out of 5 mainly because of the bugs. If I didn't experience that, I would give my experience a 4.5.

reviews.text:
We booked a small "staycation" as we live in the Phoenix area and wanted to experience some of Marriott's local offerings.

Already aware of the resort's architectural significance, we had high expectations. Our experience did not disappoint!

The resort does a great job recognizing Marriott Bonvoy status and providing perks. Check-in was smooth. Room was exceptional as we walked in. The bathrooms are VERY spacious and well-designed. Rooms are very quiet with great views. The resort looks incredible at all times of the day and is truly special to look at. Very clean room and balcony.

Room service offered a great experience. The gentleman that took our order was thorough and repeated it back. The gentleman that delivered our food set the table and created conversation with us. The grilled club was delicious, and the cheesecake was a great dessert. Presentation was spot on.

The property was great to walk around and explore, with just about any offering you may want at a resort.

The only area of improvement I noticed was signage to self-parking. It wasn't necessarily obscure, but easy to pass up. We noticed it when we looped back around.

We will definitely be returning for additional stays in the future!

reviews.text:
Our family of 6 stayed at this resort last week. When we normally check into a Marriott, we are usually warmly welcomed and thanked for our Titanium Elite status. When we pulled up to this "luxury collection" resort, we waited in a long line to check in and then we were offered upgraded rooms, then asked to pay an extra $250 per night for them. We have NEVER, in 20 years of being Elite guests, been asked to pay for an upgrade. If they are available, they should be offered to Titanium Elite members as a complimentary benefit of our status.

The rooms were big, one had a nice view of the mountain and the other looked at the roof of another building. The main pool was closed for an undisclosed amount of time, leaving only two overly crowded pools for our entire stay. Our umbrella flew out of our umbrella holder and landed in the pool, luckily not injuring anyone, but spilling water all over my phone and ruining the speakers. Why are these not more securely fastened?

For a luxury resort, I found it distasteful to host two large corporate conventions at the same time. People were constantly scatted about the hotel taking business calls, having meetings and networking. Even by the pool and spa. It felt less like I was at a luxury resort and more like I was at a WeWork. The entire time it made me feel like I had to check my email...hard to disconnect from the real world when everywhere you look you're reminded of it. Not to mention, a couple of days one of the pool was closed off to only members of the company outing...why did management think it was smart to do this when you're already down one pool? They must value companies' checkbooks more than loyal guests who pay a lot of their own money to stay there.

Tennis and Pickleball were good, the spa was way too crowded and the bikes and golf were fine.

The last thing and maybe the most important...stop advertising your hotel as a 5-star hotel when only a part of it is. If you want to stay at a 5-star hotel, you need to book at the Canyon Suites building of the Phoenician. The rest of the Phoenician is about a 3.5-star convention center.

reviews.text: This hotel is in major need of maintenance and customer service. The first issue I had was the toilet seat was broken. It took them 3 hours to come and fix it as the front desk stated they had numerous maintenance calls. I didn't get that resolved until almost 2am. The next issue is their shower was broken. Water barely came out, which is not the worst part of it. The worst part is the fact that they had a loose handle and the screw was so loose that it came out. I almost stepped on a screw while I was showering at a 5 diamond hotel. This place should be no more than a 2 diamond. Lastly, I visited their pool in the evening to notice that everyone had maintenance issues. There was tile missing everywhere and the areas it was missing, the objects were sharp. I came close to cutting myself several times against the wall so I left the pool area. AAA and Forbes, you need to revisit this place and downgrade them.

reviews.text: Just ok. There are “yes” 5 star resorts and “no” star resorts and this one is definitely a “no”. Staff does not attempt to add to the luxury experience from a service perspective, and are very quick to tell you “those are the rules” or “that’s not our policy” for even very simple requests. Unlike all other 5 stars I have been to, at this hotel you can expect to set up your own pool chairs with towels and chase down wait staff for service (with items often forgotten multiple times). No extra touches like most 5 stars such as warm or cool towels and/or a welcome drink on arrival. No greeting by name like at the other 5 stars as well. Just felt like a regular Marriott with minimal effort, and slightly nicer rooms, common spaces, and grounds. Pool area definitely felt like a Holiday Inn - it was not beautiful and I did not enjoy the ambiance while sitting at it. Food was also just ok - presentation nice enough and it was overall good but nothing to write home about. Meh. If you do chose to stay here, don’t miss the cactus garden - the best part of the hotel! The spa was also beautiful but our experience was tainted by unprofessional staff. We would not stay again and considered moving to the Arizona Biltmore halfway through but we were with family and so we stayed.  The only thing 5 star about this place was the room price.

However, the rooms are drab and depressing which is surprising for a $1k a night room. The pools and kids areas are old and need to be remodeled. They don’t have house keeping unless you specifically request it and our hot water didn’t work the last night. We switched to the JW Marriott which is much better.  The Phoenician is definitely not a 5 star hotel by any means so if you’re looking  for that quality look elsewhere.

reviews.text: Stayed in the three bedroom residence. At first impression we were very happy, but as we began to explore I was horrified at the living area couch. For a stay at $2k per night, this is unacceptable. I am a lifetime titanium elite member and have stayed in A LOT of Marriott properties. This was the most disappointed I’ve ever been. Check out the pics I attached. The icing on the cake, my wife got food poisoning! Spoke to front desk and they handed me off to the head of security? Never got a call from F & B manager. Guess this person could care less of the level of food handling in his department. Had to finally call the front desk manager at the end of the day to express grief. She was very nice and gave a $500 bill credit. I don’t ever complain at hotels and having traveled as much as I do, don’t make a big deal out of things, but comping a nights stay would have been more in line. Especially considering my poor wife was bed ridden all day and the inability to use the couch. We won’t be back. What a joke.

reviews.text: We recently visited the Phoenician for the 4th time for a girl's trip. This is a place we continue to come though it's not perfect. The spa is perfection though - every time it is just simply a day out of heaven. The spa pool could have better service - but they made it right for us, so won't say too much. The room is not really anything to write home about. It's clean but it does feel a little old and outdated and there are some non-luxury things like little stains on the carpet, chips in the furniture, etc. I really wish they would put real doors on the bathroom. Especially when you are with friends - there is no privacy to be able to use the restroom facilities. You can hear everything and there are large cracks between the shutter doors so you really don't feel like you can relax when you are showering or going to the bathroom. Maybe add a fan for noise privacy? The bathroom was mostly clean and can't really complain. You must request a room with a view - the resort view is everything! So gorgeous to sit off your balcony and look at the resort. The pools and grounds are simply amazing and the views of Camelback Mountain just can't be beat. While it's not perfect, we love going and will go again.

I booked this resort specifically to have access to the spa. I like to enjoy a nice steam/sauna and to relax. My wife likes to get massages and facials.

Upon arrival after our first night I was told by the spa I could not access the facility without having a service. I was told they were fully booked and I couldn’t even pay to access the spa facilities.

I’ve never stayed at a luxury resort and been denied access to the spa facilities as a guest on the property.

I requested a refund and promptly booked a room at The Sanctuary.

I will never stay at this hotel again. I wasn’t even offered a refund or complimentary anything for the inconvenience.

I highly recommend never staying here. You can’t even use all the facilities yet pay a premium for access to the grounds?

I got out of my car once I realized that I was actually overlooked, disregarded and not acknowledged. I asked him why he didn’t come to my car and he lied and said I wouldn’t open the car for him. I spoke to the manager and he told me that he will take my keys to the same man that refused to take my keys initially. He apologized and appeared  to be unsure how to handle the situation. He asked me if I wanted a drink. I told him that what I want is for the tape to be viewed and for him to reprimand the valet guy. I don’t want this to happen to anyone else. reviews.text:
The facility and rooms were in amazing condition. It felt brand new. The resort is beautiful and I would recommend it for a couple. Unfortunately we went with children. We were under the impression it would be good for small kids because of the splash pad and kids center. This was not the case. The resort is large and if you are not in the building close to the lobby, the pool is a long walk away. For a couple this wouldn't be a problem but when you have a stroller and pool stuff, it is a pain.  The pool is large but has zero shade. Once you are in the pool, you are cooking. No canopy or structures to provide shade over any sections of the pool. Once again, fine for adults but not children.

The staff was disappointing as well. It didn't feel like a luxury service at all. Any questions seemed to have vague answers and no one was really that helpful.  We booked a crib and confirmed during check in but it was never brought to our room until I requested a third time the next day. Another thing, I know this next one sounds very petty but how do you not have iced coffee at the pool restaurant? We were brought hot coffee over ice which just melted. Just a pet peeve lol.
We did have a valet who gave my son and I a golf cart ride around the property. My son loves golf carts and this was the best service we had the whole trip.

Another thing that was not mentioned was that the parking garage cost over 20 bucks a day. How is this not included or mentioned at check in? I would have just valeted for 2 bucks more a day. Also the TV didn't have many channels (once again we had kids with us). I was excited to see a kids package but realized they charged for it. It's just tacky when a place has everything being an extra charge.

The food was mediocre and waaaay over priced. This is normal for a resort but the food just all felt dated and wasn't that good.

Overall this would be fun for a couple or a golf trip. Just not for kids.

We have stayed at the Gainey Ranch resort and that was much much better for kids.

reviews.text: We had a nice, relaxing stay in this luxurious hotel, with some misses. The cactus garden was lovely, and the pools were nice. The room was comfortable and clean. The dining experiences were hit or miss. Lunch at the Tavern was just ok. Breakfast at Mowry and Cotton was very good, and our server Gustavo was friendly; we had nachos and drinks at the Kabobery and enjoyed some of the best guacamole we've ever had plus wonderful service. Mowry's prices were high, so our 2nd day, we got bagels, breakfast sandwiches, and coffee at the Marketplace. The staff was not as warm as that at Mowry or the Kabobery, but the food and coffee were good. The only really disappointing experience was at J&G Steakhouse. I called a few weeks before our arrival to reserve a table for a Sunday evening. I told Brianne, the woman with whom I spoke, that we were flexible on time but would like to sit outdoors (partly because of Covid and partly because the view seemed pretty). She suggested that 6:30 would be a great time to eat on the deck to for a wonderful sunset view, so I made the reservation for then. When we arrived at J&G, a few minutes early, the hostess said there were no tables outside, and an older guy who worked there said nor would there be for a long time. They were pretty snide and condescending about it. No apologies. I asked the guy if we could come back in 30-45 min and be seated outside. He chuckled derisively and said it'd be more like 90 min as all the tables were just on their appetizers. We debated leaving but didn't know where else we could go on such short notice. Our servers Rianna & Gabe were nice, but the (very $$$) steaks were overdone. We asked for medium rare and got medium, disappointing for a steakhouse. Don't have your heart set on sitting outside; please note: I wasn't told we'd be seated outdoors IF a table was available or that my request had been noted; I believed, based on my conversation, that we'd be seated there. Btw, 2 tables outside opened up within 20 minutes of when we were seated. Also we hoped to go on a guided tour of the cactus gardens; a sign read that they were given MWF at 9. We went to the concierge desk Mon before 9, and no one knew anything about a tour. Later I received a call from a staff member saying that tours were given every day at 9, except for Fri at 8. There was no one there to give a tour either Mon or Tues. The garden trails are lovely though, so just take yourself on a tour! Overall, a nice stay with some minuses.

UPDATE: You can see below that the Public Relations Director, from  the hotel, assured me that my concerns would be addressed.

Well, its been over a month and I still haven't heard anything. Leaving me no choice but to conclude that she was just blowing smoke with her well practiced  corporate response.

Is this non-response what is done to other people after givng assurances? Are you figuring that they'll blow off steam and then go away?

I tried to book through the group site as directed, without any luck. I called the rep assigned and it took multiple calls and emails to him, as well as a message for the GM, to get a response. One interesting point to note is that the GM never contacted me.                                                                            Additional, 2 miscellaneous charges, that I was not told about, for portage and room cleaning, were added to my final bill. I never used portage services. When I contacted the rep to dispute them, he indicated that they were disclosed on the booking site. Well, as mentioned, I booked with him directly, so I didn't get a chance to see them on the site. This was brought to his attention by email and it's been a month or so and he is now ignoring this fact.
I'm curious to see how quickly and deftly the customer relation person, who seems to respond to reviews,  responds to this one and spins it while showing false empathy and understanding with my dissatisfaction.

Asked Concierge to arrange tennis during my stay and they handed me a sticky note with the tennis center's extension and told me to call myself and arrange it. Valet ($38/nite) had no charger available for at the main building for our Tesla. We were told we could drive across the resort ourselves to find one in another location. No chairs available in pool area except for the 30 that were available in the "Reserved Area" where they charge $50 per chair and a $50 drink min.  Made call to tennis pro shop. No one picked up and it went to voicemail. I left messages and no one returned my call. No water available in lobby, nor coffee in the morning. At $1000 per night I expected more. We didn't even get a chocolate on our pillow or water on our nightstand. Honestly, I've gotten better treatment at far less expensive hotels. reviews.text: My wife, Lora, and I have stayed at many a fine hotel, and as Titanium members with Marriott, have grown accustomed to excellent customer service, but nothing has been as exceptional as our latest stay at the Phoenician in Arizona. From the moment we entered the resort, where we were warmly greeted by Eddie and Ryan at the front desk, who gave us a complimentary room upgrade, to the day we departed, when Charlotte in Food & Beverage gave us a complimentary fruit platter, the experience has been nothing short of exceptional. During our stay, when our flight was cancelled, Haley, a Front Desk Manager, and Jonathan, a Front Desk Agent, were kind and considerate, helping us negotiate another night, complete with a late checkout, for which we are grateful. Of course, the grounds of the resort are lovely, and the pools are amazing, but the best part of our wonderful stay has clearly been the people we had the pleasure of engaging with, so thank you to everyone at the Phoenician, you made Lora's and my 10 year anniversary exceptional, and we look forward to staying at your beautiful property again soon.

Probably my favorite hotel! I've stayed here several times in the winter and summer. Was recently here in June 2020. Pretty busy for summer but I think everyone wanted to get out and travel with COVID pretty much gone. The hotels location is amazing.

Amazing views from the rooms and of course the pools! The pools here are so nice, even if it is 115 out. Most importantly, I LOVE that they are open 24/7. Going for a swim at midnight when no one is around and the sun is not glaring down is perfect. Not many hotels I've been to have this unfortunately. The slide is really fun. Yes, I was the only adult on it that day haha.

My only negative with my last stay was the house keeping. We stayed for almost a week and they never replaced towels or toiletries like shampoo. We had to call room service who was very quick at bringing it but shouldn't have to do that.

Other than that, it's an amazing resort. The cactus garden is amazing to see with Camelback Mountain right behind. Looking forward to come back soon.

- my husband scheduled a surprise for our 20th anniversary to have strawberries, flowers, and mimosas delivered to our room upon arrival. This was not completed and he had to call them and remind them about it once we got to the room. Definitely ruined the surprise. 
-upon check in, they did not ask us about parking or add it to our room. We had to pay to get out of the parking garage a couple of days. We went back to the desk and got it added, but ultimately, it resulted in us having to pay $23 extra since they added parking on the day we had already had to self pay to get out of the garage
-I communicated via email nearly a month in advance  to request any special ideas or upgrades that might be available given our special anniversary. While this is certainly not expected, I was simply hoping the resort might offer something. I asked if they might consider a nicer room or assist me with getting a reservation for the tea luncheon. I had already tried reserving and was aware of this, but hoped for any other options…even to be on a list in case of cancellation, but nothing was offered. My wife, 6-month-old son and I stayed here over the past weekend. There are two of the residence units that are on top of each other, 7703 and 7704 with 7703 being on the ground level. We were unfortunately in 7703 for a 3-night stay and while the place is fantastic, you can hear EVERYTHING that's going on upstairs in 7704. We were just astonished at the level of noise that normal activity could make. Footsteps, talking, doors closing and opening, toilets flushing all sounded like this was happening in our own unit. This is something that I might expect from a cheap motel, but certainly not at a place like this especially given the amount of money we paid to stay there.

After the first night, we asked to be moved but they said the people upstairs were checking out and it wasn't booked for the next two nights but someone definitely checked in that afternoon. So, the normal activity upstairs continued to wake up our son during naps and at night meaning we had a very cranky 6-month-old the whole time we were there.

Other than that, everything was great. But if you check-in and they tell you that you are in 7703 of the Residences, buckle up, or ask to be in a different unit.

Our first day we checked bikes out from the fitness center and rode to downtown Scottsdale. It was a beautiful ride! That night we had drinks at the Thirsty Camel and dinner at Mawry and Cotton. Tip-get the brussel sprouts!

The next day after hiking Echo Canyon trail we spent the rest of the day in the spa. You could literally spend all day taking advantage of the services. All of us left extremely pleased with our experience and sad that it was over!

The Phoenician was conveniently located within walking distance or a short Uber ride from everything and anything we wanted to do. reviews.text:
We are local residents to the Arcadia neighborhood. We typically love the Phoenician, especially during the holiday season. We are regulars of the Tavern during football season and stay often, especially during New Years Eve. 

My husband, Erik G, married his 1st wife there, which he will gladly still share with other visiting guests during every stay. 

Sadly, the last two consecutive years we have stayed there, we have received terrible views from our rooms. 

Last year, NYE 2020, we had a view of noisy AC units from our roof top. With this poor experience and our own anniversary in mind, I wanted to make sure everything was ideal. I called and made note of our celebration, as well as our need for a beautiful view. In addition, Gloria in room service, beautifully decorated the room with rose petals, wine and chocolate covered strawberries for the occasion. (Thank you, Gloria!) I again emphasized the importance of the room location and view and asked for it to be placed in the notes prior to our check in. 

With an even deeper frustration and disappointment our view was horrible. We had views of a dumpster, multiple cardboard box pallets, what appeared to be a maintenance area and a large tree blocking any direct view of the beautiful courtyards or scenery. 

My husband did attempt to contact the front desk, asking for accommodations for another complimentary night in another room and/or a discount for a 2nd night in the same poorly positioned room. Sadly, no efforts were made to resolve the room issue, only to remove the room service bill that was billed for $224 for decorating the room with roses, wine, etc., 

Obviously, a discounted room or room with a better view would have benefited everyone, as the net result would have acquired additional dining, bar and room service expenses and rebuilt our confidence in the Phoenician (now Marriott) to future stays. 

I hope this email or survey does get to  Mark (GM) directly, as I coincidentally looked him contact information up on LinkedIn just yesterday with the intentions of following up with an email addressing my concerns. 

Feel free to publicly post and/share this survey, as I intend to do the same.

Reluctantly yours, 

Christina B.

reviews.text:
I'm a TripAdvisor so I stay frequently at hotels around the country.  We were supposed to come to The Phoenician in 2020 but COVID forced us to cancel the reservation.  We stayed at The Phoenician in early December and it was just fabulous!  We stayed in a beautiful casita which was spacious, very well laid out with a huge bathroom with double sinks, a large shower with an incredible rainfall showerhead, a separate room for the toilet and a bidet, a large walk-in closet, and a huge tub - you can't ask for anything better than that!

The bedroom had a large, movable flat-screen tv, with a large desk area for my laptop, a separate area for a "bar" area, and had a large covered patio (we were on the 2nd floor) overlooking the pools, a large green space, and the Spa - it was just very eye-pleasing.

Everything in the casita worked perfectly and it was cleaned daily.

We ate every morning at the Cotton & Mowery restaurant and the food was excellent.  I had the pancakes and they tasted just like crepes they were so soft and tasty!  The wait staff was excellent and almost every day we saw Eric Pessin, the manager who was always cheerful, friendly, and remembered our names to boot!!   The really neat thing was to see the Harris Hawk and a handler out every morning ensuring that the local birds didn't bother guests and it was cool even though they never let the hawk go, just his presence was enough to ward off the birds.

The Phoenician staff was also wonderful in remembering that we were celebrating our 33rd wedding anniversary and they had a bottle of champagne and a box of ultra-rich chocolates delivered to our room - it was touching and memorable.

We also had a wedding anniversary dinner at JG Restaurant and the food was outstanding.  

As for The Phoenician resort itself, driving in is real impressive and the magnificent water fountain at the front door is impressive.  We were encouraged to visit the Cactus Garden which we did in the daytime, but we also went back in the evening to see the lighted cactus for Christmas-time - beautiful!  The grounds are very well maintained and it was fun just walking around.

This was truly an anniversary trip that we will NEVER forget!

Definitely not a 5* experience - more of a 4* experience.

- Had to queue up for about 30 mins to check in as they only had one person at the check in desk.

- Ordered a golf cart to take me to the spa - I had to wait 30 mins to be returned back to the main lobby by the golf cart.

They are clearly understaffed.

- The rooms are very very meh - the mountain view king room was not all that at all - the view was a bit suffocating its exactly like the picture the mountain is really close up its not like a view the mountains from afar kind of vibe. Omni is 100000000% nicer.

- The service at the bar was very poor. The bar staff don't come back to you to take your order, you have to keep trying to get their attention. Our wings came out cold. They forgot our order at one point and we had to remind them of what we ordered - they comped those dishes but definitely not a 5* experience.

The attention to detail was not there as you'd expect from a high end hotel that cost $800 for one night stay.

The view is beautiful from the bar area & the hotel its self is very pretty and scenic - but I wouldn't stay again. I'd 100% recommend going to the omni instead.

P.S. I did have afternoon tea here too at a different date which was fun but I'm British and the sandwiches weren't up to par.
